correctness.rationale: The base-two factorial digit-sum identity is exact. A subset-parity lemma shows a no-carry proper multiple-of-three split exists iff s₂(3n)>=4; weights 2/3 forbid it. For three bits of one parity, an explicit two-plus-two-bit split attains valuation 1. For two bits of opposite parity, every split has at least two bits in each multiple of three and explicit decompositions attain valuation 2, separately treating adjacent exponents. This covers all n>=2 without computational inference. Actual verifier replays exact binomial GCDs for n<=200 and carry minima/witnesses for n<=1000.

originality.rationale: Three highly relevant complete primary preprints were compared statement-by-statement. McTague gives a congruence-restricted valuation theorem and only the first exceptional (2,3,6) example; Wu handles distinct prime cases and special m=2; Fairfax-Ball proves the sharp global bound 2 and first equality row but no binary-weight row classification. Six claim-specific searches in publicly available mathematical research records and exact-formulation, parameter, OEIS and broader-coverage searches found no equivalent or stronger theorem. Unindexed results remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed earlier exact characterization of the ternary-step, prime-two family could exist; claim-specific web, OEIS, indexed research records and the closest three full primary texts revealed none.
An additional 2025 related restricted-GCD paper was compared only at abstract level; its advertised index restriction differs and is not a decisive unresolved comparison.

value.rationale: The step-three, p=2 case is a mathematically forced first exception to the congruence hypotheses of the classical selected-binomial GCD theorem, explicitly flagged by McTague’s v₂(binomial(6,3))=2 example. The 2026 uniform sharp bound 2 still leaves pointwise values unknown. The new infinite, complete digit-weight classification establishes exactly when the entire family is odd, divisible by 2 but not 4, or divisible by 4, with explicit structural carry witnesses. It closes a natural local valuation gap rather than a one-off tabulation or routine numerical increment.
